label: Atoms to tokens and back
context: A strip of about 40 atoms (small dots, coloured by residue in alternating light shades) belonging to 8 tokens (residues). Phase 1 'atom encoder': local attention windows: a highlighted window of query atoms (one block) connects with thin lines to a wider surrounding window of key atoms; caption 'local attention: 32 query atoms see 128 neighbours'; the window slides along. Phase 2: atoms of each residue merge (animate dots flowing together) into 8 larger token circles; caption 'aggregate atoms → tokens'. Phase 3 'token transformer': all 8 tokens attend globally (arrows between all), with a faint pair-bias grid z overlaid modulating arrow thickness; caption 'global attention, biased by the pair representation z'. Phase 4 'atom decoder': tokens split back into atoms, each atom gets a small coordinate update arrow. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Atoms to tokens and back
spec.caption: A 14 s loop of the denoiser: atom encoder (local attention), aggregation into 8 tokens, global token attention biased by z, then the decoder splits tokens back into atoms with a coordinate update each. Window sizes are drawn scaled down.
